description: The entrance to culture, plus ritual and its institutions. Language, art, music, history, religion, Taoism, and emotion are their own clusters.

concepts.title: Culture
concepts.summary: Meaning survives by changing. A story, a ritual, a word carries the marks of every hand it passed through, and each generation feels it from the inside, as if it had always been this way.

concepts.title: Ritual
concepts.summary: Repeated actions that mean more than they do. Lighting a candle, sharing a meal, raising a hand. A ritual lets a community hold a feeling steady long enough to share it.

concepts.title: Institutions
concepts.summary: Repeat a ritual long enough and rules, roles, and buildings grow around it. Institutions are memory made durable, and sometimes made rigid.

concepts.title: Festivals
concepts.summary: Shared time set aside from ordinary time: harvests, new years, saints' days. They mark the calendar, bind a community, and give people a reason to gather that isn't work.

concepts.title: Funerals
concepts.summary: Almost every culture has a way of saying goodbye to the dead. The forms differ enormously, but the job is the same: to mark the loss, gather the living, and let the grief have somewhere to go.

concepts.title: Food
concepts.summary: Fuel that became language. What people eat, when, and with whom carries memory, belonging, and identity, and a shared meal is possibly the oldest ritual there is.
